metadata.title: Hypervelocity Star Candidates in the SEGUE G & K Dwarf Sample

evidence.quote:
We report a set of 20 hypervelocity candidates from
the SEGUE G and K dwarf sample. These candidates
have velocities greatly exceeding the escape velocity at
their respective positions in the Galaxy, albeit with large
proper-motion errors.

notes: HVS 3 (J160620.65+042451.5) and HVS 20 (J145132.12+003258.0): Table 1 (T:p7-b0) reports 34.88% and 43.24% bound probabilities, respectively, but the authors retain both in the final 20-candidate HVS sample (T:p3-b11, T:p7-b2). The IAU-name spacing around the sign in Table 1 is normalized in the identifier values.

HVS 1: At T:p7-b0 (Table 1), only the total proper motion is listed for HVS 1 (56.1 mas/yr); separate proper-motion components are not reported, so proper_motion_ra and proper_motion_dec are omitted. The equatorial coordinates are not tabulated separately; ra and dec are decoded from the IAU name J060306.77+825829.1 in Table 1. The Galactic rest-frame speed is represented by the Table 1 total velocity v^d and minimum total velocity v_min, whose definitions are given in footnotes d and e. No parallax or Galactocentric radius is reported for this star. The paper reports % Bound only, not a separate unbound probability.

HVS 2: Table 1 lists the total proper motion v_t = 15.7 mas/yr for HVS 2, but not separate RA and Dec proper-motion components, so proper_motion_ra and proper_motion_dec are not extracted. The table reports % Bound = 7.43; an unbound probability is not explicitly reported. The v^d value is retained as the paper's total Galactic Cartesian velocity; the table note defines it as the total velocity after conversion to that frame before error consideration.

HVS 3: Table 1 row 3 corresponds to HVS 3 / J160620.65+042451.5. The table does not list separate RA/Dec values or separate proper-motion components; the coordinates are encoded in the IAU designation, and the listed vt=23.7 mas/yr is the total proper motion rather than an equatorial component. The tabulated total speed v=641.8 km/s is the present-day value before error consideration; the table also lists v_min=195.1 km/s from Monte Carlo realizations, but that is a minimum over error realizations rather than the present-day state, so it is not separately recorded.

HVS 4: Target: HVS 4 = J113102.87+665751.1 (a "Reliable" proper-motion candidate; among the three most unbound candidates in Fig. 2). The paper does not tabulate right ascension and declination separately; they appear only within the IAU designation, so they are reported here in the sexagesimal form given, with mixed units noted (RA in hourangle h m s, Dec in deg arcmin arcsec); no conversion was performed since conversions are not allowed.
